feature: The Sunfish's rubrail is a vinyl rail's section (flat crowned face, rounded corners, 22 mm tall, about 15 mm proud) seated on the topsides, in place of a 22 mm round tube.
features: drail() in build_fleet.py: a section swept along the round-4 rail path (unchanged): back leaning in with the topsides' flare (0.26 per metre) and 1-2 mm inside them, flat face crowned 1 mm, 4 mm corners, top 1 mm under the deck's edge so the joint shows as a line
the ends beside the rudder's fittings close off over their last 12 mm (end sections scaled 0.6 about the back); caps face outward (Mesh.v mirrors y, so they wind the other way from tube()'s)
references: Round 4's blind reviewers and QA (the rail thin); Bean's pick Nov 14 ("Thicker rubrail"). A 1-1/16 x 11/16 in flexible vinyl rail is the common profile for 10-16 ft boats (Taco Marine, RecPro catalogues).
mac_note: No game code changes. The Mac rebakes and reimports the Sunfish (the Sunfish's meshes only, not the shared kit), then the boats gate.
findings: Blind A/B round 1 (27 mm D-section, 22 mm proud): 2 of 3 picked it, all three said it was too big and bumper-like.

QA round 1: a 4.5 mm wedge gap between the rail's vertical back and the flared topsides, and both end caps facing inward (the old tube()'s caps do too). Fixed: the back leans with the flare (every back point 0.8-8 mm inside the hull), caps reversed (dot 0.90 outward).
Blind A/B round 2 on the slimmer rail (fresh reviewers): 3 of 3 (realism, boatbuilder, 3D artist) picked it.
QA round 2: 0 non-manifold edges, no folds at the corners or the closed ends, 23.6 mm clear of the rudder and 15.0 mm of the fittings; only the comment's numbers were off (fixed).
Volume, CB, LOA, beam, fairness (0 inflections) and seams unchanged; 121,626 to 124,558 triangles.

Open: the rail stops 45 mm either side of the centreline at the transom for the rudder's fittings (reviewers would like it to run behind the gudgeon's plate or end in a moulded cap); no shadow reveal under its lower edge; tube() still has inward caps on other boats.
